prompt: Bona orally placed an order for two (2) pairs of Bikini, Bikini One and Bikini Two she needs for the BB. Laguna beauty contest to be held on April 1, 2026 at the garment factory of Tin. Tin does not regularly manufacture for the general market Bikini One but Tin regularly manufactures Bikini Two but was still in the factory at that time. Tin agreed to deliver on March 30, 2026 and Bona agreed to pay upon delivery to her at the quoted price of P8,000 for each Bikini. As a result, which of the following is correct?

choices.text: The contracts for Bikini One and Bikini Two are both enforceable
The contracts for Bikini One and Bikini Two are both unenforceable
Only the contract for Bikini One is enforceable
Only the contract for Bikini Two is enforceable

rationale: Under Art. 1467, goods manufactured specially for the buyer and not fit for sale to others in the ordinary course of business are not subject to the Statute of Frauds requirement of a note or memorandum, unlike goods that the manufacturer regularly makes for the general market. Since Tin does not regularly manufacture Bikini One (a special order not readily saleable to others), that oral contract is enforceable outright; Bikini Two, which Tin regularly manufactures for the general market, remains subject to the Statute of Frauds (Art. 1403[2][d]) and, absent a note/memorandum, delivery, or payment at this point, is unenforceable.

source.center: CPA Review School of the Philippines (CPAR)

canonicalConcept: A contract for goods specially manufactured for the buyer, not ordinarily saleable to others, falls outside the Statute of Frauds and is enforceable even if oral, unlike a contract for the seller's regular stock-in-trade goods.

prompt: Using the facts in no. 1, if Tin fails to deliver Bikini One on March 30, 2026, which of the following is not correct?

choices.text: Tin is guilty of delay despite absence of demand
Tin will be liable for damages because the contract is enforceable
There is no delay because there was no demand made by Bona
Bona can be compelled to effect delivery and is also liable for damages

rationale: Under Art. 1169, demand is generally necessary to constitute delay, EXCEPT when time is of the essence of the obligation, as expressly or impliedly shown by the circumstances (here, the bikini was needed for a specific beauty contest date, making the March 30 delivery date essential to the purpose of the contract). Because time is of the essence, Tin incurs delay automatically upon failure to deliver on the due date, without need of demand — making the statement that 'there is no delay because there was no demand' the incorrect one.

source.center: CPA Review School of the Philippines (CPAR)

canonicalConcept: Delay may arise automatically upon the due date, without need of demand, when time is of the essence of the obligation as shown by the surrounding circumstances.

prompt: Using the facts in no. 1, if Tin delivers Bikini Two on March 30, 2026, which of the following is correct?

choices.text: Bona should pay the agreed price of P8,000.
Bona can refuse to accept the delivery even if Tin observed the specification required by Bona
Tin can require Bona to pay damages if Bona refuses to accept without valid reason.
Tin can go to court to compel Bona to pay P8,000 plus damages

rationale: Since the oral contract for Bikini Two remains unenforceable under the Statute of Frauds until ratified by delivery AND acceptance by the buyer (or by a note/memorandum or partial payment), Bona retains the right to refuse the mere tender of delivery; the contract is only cured and becomes enforceable once Bona actually accepts and receives the goods. Until such acceptance, Bona's refusal is not actionable, and Tin cannot yet compel payment or claim damages for the refusal.

source.center: CPA Review School of the Philippines (CPAR)

canonicalConcept: An unenforceable oral contract for the seller's regular stock-in-trade goods (covered by the Statute of Frauds) is cured only by the buyer's actual acceptance and receipt of the goods; before that, the buyer may still validly refuse the tendered delivery.

prompt: May, Ting, Gil and Luz are partners in a Universal Partnership of present property. Thereafter they acquired property as follows: I. May, an agricultural land by inheritance; II. Ting, a coconut plantation by donation; III. Gil, a condominium unit by purchase; IV. Luz, pieces of Jewelry by legacy. Which of the following statements is correct?

choices.text: I, II, III, IV will belong to the partnership
III will belong to the partnership
I, II, IV will belong to May, Ting and Luz respectively
None will belong to the partnership

rationale: Under Art. 1779, in a universal partnership of all present property, only the property already owned by the partners at the time of constitution (and profits therefrom) becomes common property; property subsequently acquired by a partner through inheritance, legacy, or donation is expressly EXCLUDED from the partnership even by stipulation, except only the fruits thereof. Property acquired by PURCHASE after constitution is likewise the acquiring partner's own, absent an express stipulation making subsequently acquired property common. Since May's, Ting's, and Luz's acquisitions (inheritance, donation, legacy) are expressly excluded by law, and Gil's condominium (acquired by purchase) is not shown to be covered by any stipulation extending the partnership to subsequently acquired property, none of the four properties belongs to the partnership.

source.center: CPA Review School of the Philippines (CPAR)

canonicalConcept: In a universal partnership of all present property, property subsequently acquired by inheritance, legacy, or donation is expressly excluded from the partnership even by stipulation, and purchased property likewise remains the partner's own absent an express stipulation extending the partnership's coverage.

prompt: In a Universal Partnership of Profits. Which of the following statements is correct?

choices.text: The loss of the property contributed by a partner shall be borne by the partnership
The loss of the property contributed by a partner shall be borne by the partner who contributed such property
The ownership of the property contributed by a partner is retained by such partner
Any property acquired thereafter by a partner shall belong to the partnership.

rationale: Under Art. 1780-1781, in a universal partnership of PROFITS, only the usufruct (use and profits) of the partners' present property is transferred to the partnership; ownership of the property itself is retained by the contributing partner. Consequently, the partnership only acquires the fruits/profits from the property, and property subsequently acquired by a partner (other than through his industry or while the partnership subsists) belongs to that partner individually, not the partnership.

source.center: CPA Review School of the Philippines (CPAR)

canonicalConcept: In a universal partnership of profits, only the usufruct of the partners' present property passes to the partnership; ownership is retained by the contributing partner himself.

prompt: Under the Revised Corporation Code, preferred shares

choices.text: May either be with par or no par
Shall have voting rights
Must be with par
Must be without par

rationale: Under the RCC (Sec. 6) and SEC regulations, preferred shares must always have a par value; the option to issue no-par value shares is available only for common shares, not preferred shares, since the preferences (e.g., as to assets or dividends) attached to preferred shares are typically expressed relative to a par value.

source.center: CPA Review School of the Philippines (CPAR)

canonicalConcept: Under Philippine corporate law, preferred shares must always be issued with a par value, unlike common shares which may be issued as no-par value shares.

prompt: Cris L, Cris G and Cris V are partners in three (3) C Spa and Massage Parlor contributing P50m, P30m and P20m, respectively. They agreed that Cris L shall be the managing partner. The business is lucrative and profitable and has many, happy customers due to their friendly, beautiful and accommodating women attendants who are willing to render extra service for customers' satisfaction. Later, an entrapment operation was conducted by government agents and caught some women attendants and customers engage in sexual congress. As a consequence, the government shall confiscate

choices.text: The contribution of the partners
The profits realized by the partnership
Both the profits and the contribution
Both the assets and the profits

rationale: Under Art. 1770, a partnership formed for an unlawful purpose is void, and the profits obtained from that unlawful business shall be confiscated in favor of the government; however, the original CONTRIBUTIONS of the partners (their capital) are to be returned/refunded to them, since only the illicit profits (fruits of the illegal activity), not the partners' own invested capital, are subject to confiscation.

source.center: CPA Review School of the Philippines (CPAR)

canonicalConcept: When a partnership is engaged in an unlawful business, only the profits realized from that illegal activity are confiscated in favor of the government; the partners' original capital contributions are returned to them.

prompt: Non-voting shares can vote

choices.text: Mortgage or pledge of corporate property
Investment in another corporation
Increasing indebtedness of the corporation
Declaration of cash dividend

rationale: Under Sec. 6 of the RCC, holders of non-voting shares are nonetheless entitled to vote on certain fundamental corporate matters, including investment of corporate funds in another corporation or business (as well as amendment of the articles of incorporation, adoption/amendment of by-laws, sale or disposition of all or substantially all corporate assets, incurring/increasing/decreasing bonded indebtedness, merger or consolidation, dissolution, and other matters enumerated by law) — a mortgage or pledge of corporate property, an increase of ordinary (non-bonded) indebtedness, and declaration of cash dividends are ordinary board matters not requiring a vote even of holders of non-voting shares.

source.center: CPA Review School of the Philippines (CPAR)

canonicalConcept: Holders of non-voting shares retain the right to vote on specific fundamental corporate acts enumerated in Sec. 6 of the RCC, such as investing corporate funds in another corporation, even though they cannot vote on ordinary corporate matters.

prompt: Will require stockholders approval

choices.text: Amendment of by laws
Contract with its own Director
Declaration of dividend
Management contract

rationale: Under Sec. 43 of the RCC, a management contract between a corporation and another corporation (or person) requires the approval of the board of both contracting corporations AND the stockholders/members owning at least a majority of the outstanding capital stock (or a higher 2/3 vote if certain interlocking-interest conditions are present); by contrast, amendment of by-laws may in some instances be delegated to the board, an ordinary self-dealing director's contract meeting the RCC's safe-harbor conditions needs no stockholder vote, and declaration of dividends is generally a board prerogative alone (except stock dividends, which need stockholder approval).

source.center: CPA Review School of the Philippines (CPAR)

canonicalConcept: A management contract between corporations requires the approval of both companies' boards and, additionally, the affirmative vote of stockholders owning at least a majority of the outstanding capital stock.

prompt: Who fills-up vacancy in the Board? A. Stockholders if the Board has no quorum. B. Board, if remaining members constitute a quorum

choices.text: Both A and B are correct
Both A and B are wrong
Only A is correct
Only B is correct

rationale: Statement A is correct: under Sec. 28 of the RCC, when the board no longer has a quorum, any vacancy must be filled by the stockholders/members themselves in a meeting called for that purpose. Statement B, however, overstates the rule as an unqualified entitlement — Sec. 28 makes board-level filling merely permissive ('may be filled by the remaining directors'), available only for vacancies other than removal or expiration of term, and does not foreclose the stockholders from instead filling the vacancy themselves even when a quorum remains; stated as an absolute rule, Statement B is therefore not strictly accurate.

source.center: CPA Review School of the Philippines (CPAR)

canonicalConcept: A board vacancy is always properly filled by the stockholders when no quorum remains; but board-level filling by the remaining directors, while permitted when a quorum remains and the vacancy is not from removal or expiration of term, is a permissive option rather than an absolute rule.

prompt: Every person has no insurable interest in the life and health of:

choices.text: himself
his parents
his girlfriend
his debtor

rationale: Under the Insurance Code, a person is presumed to have an unlimited insurable interest in his own life and health, and in the life of persons on whom he is dependent for support/education (such as parents), or to whom he owes an obligation (such as a debtor, to the extent of the debt, and a creditor in the life of the debtor). A mere romantic relationship (girlfriend), without more (e.g., without a legally recognized dependency, pecuniary interest, or family relation), does not by itself create an insurable interest recognized under the Insurance Code.

source.center: CPA Review School of the Philippines (CPAR)

canonicalConcept: Insurable interest in another's life requires a recognized basis such as blood/family relation, financial dependency, or a pecuniary interest such as a debt owed; a mere romantic relationship alone does not establish insurable interest.

prompt: Which of the following statement is not correct?

choices.text: An insurer may procure another person to insure him against loss or liability by reason of an original insurance.
A contract of reinsurance is presumed to be a contract of indemnity and not purely against damage.
The original insured has no interest in contract of reinsurance.
A contract of reinsurance exists where the same person is insured by several insurers separately in respect to the same subject and interest.

rationale: Choice (d) describes DOUBLE INSURANCE (where the same person insures the same subject and interest with several insurers), not reinsurance. Reinsurance, by contrast, is a contract whereby an insurer (the ceding insurer) procures a THIRD insurer to insure it against loss or liability by reason of the original insurance it issued to the original insured — the original insured has no interest in, and is not a party to, this reinsurance arrangement.

source.center: CPA Review School of the Philippines (CPAR)

canonicalConcept: Reinsurance is a separate contract between the original insurer and a reinsurer covering the insurer's own risk under the original policy, in which the original insured has no interest, distinct from double insurance where the same insured obtains multiple policies from several insurers over the same risk.

prompt: Exception under the foreign currency deposit secrecy law:

choices.text: When there is written permission of the depositor.
Upon under of a competent court in cases of bribery.
Where the money deposited or invested is the subject matter of the litigation.
In cases of dereliction of duty of public officials.

rationale: Under RA 6426 (Foreign Currency Deposit Act), the confidentiality of foreign currency deposits is ABSOLUTE and admits of only ONE exception: upon the WRITTEN PERMISSION of the depositor. Unlike the peso deposit secrecy law (RA 1405), foreign currency deposits are not subject to inquiry even in cases of bribery, dereliction of duty of public officials, or litigation involving the money deposited, absent the depositor's own written consent.

source.center: CPA Review School of the Philippines (CPAR)

canonicalConcept: Foreign currency deposits enjoy absolute confidentiality under RA 6426, subject only to the depositor's own written permission, unlike peso deposits which have several statutory exceptions to secrecy.

prompt: As a requirement in registration with the Cooperative Development Authority, in no case shall the paid-up share capital be less than
rationale: Under the Cooperative Code and CDA implementing rules, for a cooperative to be registered, its paid-up share capital must in no case be less than Fifteen Thousand Pesos (P15,000), ensuring a minimum capital base before the cooperative can be recognized as a going concern.

source.center: CPA Review School of the Philippines (CPAR)

canonicalConcept: The Cooperative Development Authority requires a minimum paid-up share capital of P15,000 before a cooperative may be registered.

prompt: Spouses A and B died leaving a mango orchard to their 2 sons, W and Y who later made an extrajudicial settlement giving the administration of the mango orchard to W and to divide the net harvest equally. Which of the following is correct?

choices.text: W and Y are partners and will report their respective share in the net harvest as part of taxable income
W and Y are not partners and will not report their respective share in the net harvest as part of taxable income
W and Y are partners and their respective share in the net harvest will be subject to final tax
W and Y are not partners, and the income of the partnership is not taxable

rationale: Co-ownership arising from inheritance, where the heirs simply preserve and hold the inherited property in common (with mere administration of the co-owned property and division of the resulting income) without deliberately investing the profits in any additional business, does NOT create a partnership under Art. 1769(2) — co-ownership does not itself establish a partnership even where the co-owners share the profits made by the use of the property they co-own. Since W and Y remain mere co-owners, not partners, there is no separate taxable partnership entity, and while their individual shares of income remain part of their own respective taxable income under general income tax rules, the joint venture/co-ownership itself is not a taxable partnership.

source.center: CPA Review School of the Philippines (CPAR)

canonicalConcept: Heirs who merely preserve and administer inherited property in common, dividing the income without deliberately reinvesting it in a new business, remain co-owners rather than partners, so no separate taxable partnership arises.

prompt: A, B, C and D are partners contributing Php 10,000, Php 20,000, Php 30,000 and Php 40,000 respectively. A, B and D are the general partners while C is the limited partner. If only Php 30,000 assets remain and the partnership has unpaid obligations to Y – Php 50,000, to partner B – Php 30,000 and to partner C – Php 20,000. Which of the following is correct if there is no profit and loss sharing agreement?

choices.text: Y collects Php 30,000 from the partnership and Php 5,000 each from partners A, B, C and D
C is exempt from loss hence, he can recover the Php 20,000 obligation of the partnership to him from either A, B or D
The Php 20,000 obligation of the partnership to C can be used to offset C's capital deficiency
Y collects Php 30,000 from the partnership and the balance of Php 20,000 will be collected from A, B and D in equal share

rationale: Under Art. 1839's order of priority in partnership liquidation, outside creditors (like Y) are paid ahead of partners' claims. The remaining P30,000 partnership assets go first to Y, leaving a P20,000 deficiency; since a limited partner (C) is not personally liable to outside creditors beyond his capital contribution, this deficiency must be satisfied by the GENERAL partners (A, B, and D), who under Art. 1816 are liable pro rata (in equal shares, as among themselves for firm debts to third persons) with their separate property for the unpaid balance.

source.center: CPA Review School of the Philippines (CPAR)

canonicalConcept: In partnership liquidation, outside creditors are paid first from partnership assets, and any deficiency is chargeable pro rata (in equal shares) against the separate property of the general partners only, since a limited partner is not personally liable to outside creditors beyond his capital contribution.

prompt: Which of the following statements is correct?

choices.text: If the thing pledged is returned by the pledgee to the pledgor, the obligation is extinguished
In sale at public auction, the pledgor may bid and his bid is valid even if he is the only bidder
Any stipulation authorizing the pledgee to appropriate the thing pledged is valid and will be given effect
Shares of stock cannot be the object of pledge or mortgage

rationale: Under Art. 2112, at the public sale of a pledged thing, the debtor/pledgor is not precluded from bidding, and his bid, even if he is the only bidder, is valid and binding. (Choice a is false — Art. 2110 provides that if the thing pledged is returned to the pledgor or owner, it extinguishes the PLEDGE, but the underlying principal obligation remains; choice c is false — Art. 2088 declares any pactum commissorium/stipulation allowing the pledgee to appropriate the thing pledged VOID; choice d is false — shares of stock are personal property and may validly be the object of a pledge or chattel mortgage.)

source.center: CPA Review School of the Philippines (CPAR)

canonicalConcept: At a pledge's public foreclosure sale, the pledgor-debtor may validly bid on the thing pledged, even as the sole bidder, unlike a pactum commissorium clause allowing outright appropriation by the pledgee, which is void.

prompt: A, B and C are partners in a joint venture engaged in real estate and land development. A, without the knowledge of B and C offered to sell to D all the remaining unsold lots at a price very much higher than the prevailing market prices. Later, A bought out B and C from the partnership and thereafter finally sold all the lots at very big profits. Statement 1 – When A bought out B and C from the partnership, the partnership was dissolved so B and C have no more share in the profit of the sale. Statement 2 – The sale of the lots between A and D is void because it was without the knowledge and consent of B and C

choices.text: True, true
True, false
False, true
False, false

rationale: Statement 1 is false: while A's buy-out of B and C dissolves the partnership as to them, the sale to D was already offered/perfected as a partnership transaction (in the ordinary course of the partnership's real estate business under Art. 1818, binding the partnership even without unanimous knowledge) before the buy-out, so B and C retain a right to share in the resulting profit as an unfinished partnership transaction, not extinguished merely by their subsequent buy-out. Statement 2 is also false: a partner's act of apparently carrying on the usual business of the partnership (here, selling real estate lots, the very business of the joint venture) binds the partnership even without the actual knowledge/consent of the other partners, as long as the third person (D) had no notice of any restriction on A's authority; hence the sale is not void.

source.center: CPA Review School of the Philippines (CPAR)

canonicalConcept: A partner's sale of partnership property in the partnership's ordinary line of business binds the firm under apparent authority even without the other partners' actual knowledge, and a subsequent buy-out of the other partners does not extinguish their right to share in profits from a transaction already underway.

prompt: A and B are solidarily obliged to give a brand new Corolla Altis valued at Php 1M to C. C demands delivery from A and B but they failed to deliver the car because their money is not enough as A only had Php 50,000 while B only had Php 500,000. As a result, C can Statement 1 – Ask from either A or B the delivery of the car plus damages. Statement 2- Ask from A the delivery of the car plus damages. Statement 3- Ask from B the delivery of the car without damages

choices.text: All statements are correct
All statements are wrong
Only two statements are correct
Only one statement is correct

rationale: In a solidary obligation to deliver a determinate/specific thing, if the debtors fail to deliver through their fault, the creditor may proceed against ANY of the solidary debtors for the full obligation PLUS damages, since each solidary debtor answers for the entire obligation, including any resulting liability for damages arising from the breach (Art. 1207-1216, 1170). Statement 1 (asking from EITHER A or B for the car plus damages) is correct, and Statement 2 (asking specifically from A for the car plus damages) is likewise a valid, correct application of that same rule — naming A specifically does not make it wrong, since A is one of the solidary debtors and remains liable for the thing and damages. Only Statement 3 is incorrect, since it wrongly suggests B could be held liable for the object WITHOUT damages, when in truth damages attach regardless of which solidary debtor is proceeded against.

source.center: CPA Review School of the Philippines (CPAR)

canonicalConcept: In a solidary obligation, a creditor may demand the entire performance plus any resulting damages from any one of the solidary debtors, including from one specifically named among them; only a version of the claim that improperly excludes damages is incorrect.

prompt: A, desiring to buy a certain property, hired an expert to ascertain its true value. But the expert's opinion turned out to be wrong and A, the buyer, was therefore misled. May A ask for the annulment of the contract?

choices.text: Yes, because the opinion was made by an expert
No, a mere expression of an opinion does not signify fraud
No, because A's own expert committed the error
Yes, A has relied on the expert's special knowledge

rationale: Under Art. 1341, a mere expression of an opinion, even by an expert, does not signify fraud sufficient to vitiate consent, unless made by an expert WITH INTENT TO DECEIVE and relied upon by the OTHER party. Here, the expert who erred was A's OWN hired agent — not an expert engaged or presented by the seller — so there is no fraud imputable to the seller at all; the error is entirely A's own risk to bear precisely because it was A's own chosen expert who made the mistake, not because expert opinions are categorically incapable of constituting fraud.

source.center: CPA Review School of the Philippines (CPAR)

canonicalConcept: Where the erring expert was hired by the very buyer who claims to have been misled, any resulting error is that buyer's own risk to bear, since no fraud attributable to the seller exists in the first place.

prompt: ABC Corporation issued redeemable shares. Under the terms of the issuance, the shares shall be redeemed at the end of 10years from date of issuance at par value plus a premium of 10%. Choose the correct statement relating to these redeemable shares.

choices.text: ABC Corporation would need unrestricted retained earnings to be able to redeem the shares
Corporations are not allowed to issue redeemable shares; thus, the issuance by ABC Corporation is ultra vires act
Holders of redeemable shares enjoy a preference over creditors
ABC Corporation may redeem the shares at the end of 10 years without need for unrestricted retained earnings provided that, after the redemption, there are sufficient assets to cover its debts

rationale: Under the RCC and SEC rules, redeemable shares may be redeemed by the corporation regardless of the existence of unrestricted retained earnings, provided that after such redemption, the corporation still has sufficient assets to cover its debts and liabilities, including capital stock, so as not to defraud its creditors — a special exception to the trust fund doctrine that otherwise requires unrestricted retained earnings for share repurchases.

source.center: CPA Review School of the Philippines (CPAR)

canonicalConcept: Redeemable shares may be redeemed even without unrestricted retained earnings, provided the corporation remains solvent enough to cover its debts and liabilities after the redemption.

prompt: Letter of Credit are financial devices in commercial transactions which will ensure that the seller of the goods is sure to be paid when he parts with the goods and the buyer of the goods gets control of the goods upon payment. Which statement is most accurate?

choices.text: The use of the letter of credit serves to reduce the risk of non-payment of the purchase price in a sale transaction
The letter of credit can only be used exclusively in a sales transaction
The letter of credit are issued for the benefits of the seller only
A, B and Care all correct

rationale: A letter of credit is essentially a financing/payment-assurance device that reduces the risk of non-payment for the seller/beneficiary in a commercial transaction; it is not exclusively limited to sales transactions (it is also used in various other commercial/trade financing arrangements) and it serves the interests of both the buyer (who obtains control of the goods upon payment/presentation of documents) and the seller (who is assured of payment), not the seller alone.

source.center: CPA Review School of the Philippines (CPAR)

canonicalConcept: A letter of credit primarily functions to reduce the risk of non-payment in commercial transactions, benefiting both buyer and seller, and is not confined solely to sales transactions.

prompt: X the President of ZZZ Corporation was authorized by the Board of Directors of ZZZ Corporation to obtain loan from YYY Bank and to sign documents in behalf of the corporation. X personally negotiated for the loan and got the loan at very low interest rates. Upon maturity of the loan, ZZZ Corporation was unable to pay. Which statement is most accurate?

choices.text: Because X was personally acting in behalf of the Corporation, he can be held personally liable
X, as President, cannot be personally held liable for the obligation of the corporation even though he signed all the loan documents, because the loan was authorized by the Board
YYY Bank can choose as to who it wants to hold liable for the loan
If ZZZ Corporation cannot pay, X can be held subsidiarily liable

rationale: Since X acted strictly within the scope of authority duly granted by the Board (a valid corporate act), X is merely an agent of the corporation, and the loan obligation is that of the corporation itself, not X personally; under basic agency and corporate law principles, an officer who signs a contract on behalf of, and within the authority granted by, the corporation is not personally liable for the corporation's resulting obligations.

source.center: CPA Review School of the Philippines (CPAR)

canonicalConcept: A corporate officer who signs documents strictly within the authority validly granted by the board acts merely as the corporation's agent and is not personally liable for the resulting corporate obligation.

prompt: X owns 99% of the capital stock of SSS Corporation. X also owns 99% of TTT Corporation. SSS Corporation obtained a loan from VVV Bank. On due date, SSS Corporation defaulted. TTT Corporation is financially healthy. Which statement is accurate?

choices.text: X, being a controlling owner of SSS Corporation can automatically be held personally liable for the loan of SSS Corporation
TTT Corporation, owned 99% by X, can automatically he held liable

SSS Corporation and TTT Corporation, although both are owned by X, are two distinct corporations with separate juridical personalities. Hence, the TTT Corporation cannot automatically be held liable for the loan of SSS Corporation
The principle of piercing the veil of corporation fiction can be applied in this case

rationale: Mere ownership of shares in two corporations by the same person does not, by itself, justify disregarding their separate juridical personalities; SSS Corporation and TTT Corporation remain distinct entities with their own rights and liabilities, so TTT Corporation cannot automatically be held liable for SSS Corporation's debt absent proof of fraud, alter ego relationship, or other recognized grounds for piercing the corporate veil, none of which is shown on these facts.

source.center: CPA Review School of the Philippines (CPAR)

canonicalConcept: Common ownership of two corporations by the same stockholder does not, by itself, justify disregarding their separate juridical personalities or holding one liable for the other's debts.

prompt: XXX Corporation and YYY Corporation have agreed to be merged into one corporate. To facilitate the merger, both corporations agreed that the merger be made effective on May 31, 2023. The SEC approved the Articles of Merger on June 30, 2023. Which statement is most accurate?

choices.text: The effective date of the merger is May 31, 2023, the date stipulated by the parties as the effective date
The effective date of the merger is always the date of the approval of the Articles of Merger by the SEC
The effective date of the merger would be the date approved by the Board of Directors and the stockholders
The stockholders and the Board of Directors can set the effective date of the merger any time after the approval of the SEC

rationale: Under the RCC, a merger or consolidation takes effect only upon the ISSUANCE by the SEC of a certificate of merger or consolidation approving the Articles of Merger; parties cannot validly stipulate an earlier effective date, since the merger's legal effect (the constituent corporations' dissolution and the transfer of their assets/liabilities) requires the SEC's approval to take place.

source.center: CPA Review School of the Philippines (CPAR)

canonicalConcept: A merger or consolidation of corporations becomes effective only upon the SEC's approval and issuance of the certificate of merger/consolidation, regardless of any earlier effective date the parties may have stipulated.

prompt: X is a minority stockholder of CC Corporation. Y is a member of the Board of Directors of CCC Corporation and at the same time he is the President. X believes that Y is mismanaging CCC Corporation hence, as a stockholder and in behalf of the other stockholders, he wanted to sue Y. Which statement is most accurate?

choices.text: X can institute a derivative suit in behalf of himself as a stockholder
A derivative suit must be instituted in behalf of the corporation
Derivative suit is an exclusive remedy that X can institute
Derivative suit is not the remedy in this situation

rationale: A derivative suit is an action brought by a stockholder in behalf of and for the benefit of the CORPORATION, to redress wrongs committed against it (such as mismanagement by its own director/officer) when the corporation itself, being controlled by the wrongdoers, fails or refuses to sue; any recovery in a derivative suit accrues to the corporation, not to the suing stockholder personally.

source.center: CPA Review School of the Philippines (CPAR)

canonicalConcept: A derivative suit is brought by a stockholder on behalf of the corporation itself to redress wrongs committed against it, with any recovery accruing to the corporation rather than to the stockholder personally.

prompt: X maintains a savings deposit in the amount of Php 1M with ABC Bank Corporation. X also has obtained a loan from ABC Bank Corporation in the amount of Php 1M. In case of default

choices.text: ABC Bank can set-off the loan from the savings account being maintained by X with ABC Bank
Set-off is not possible because legal compensation is not allowed in banking transaction
Deposit accounts are usually earmarked for specific purpose hence, off-setting is not legally possible
Off-setting is not possible because the obligation of X is a "simple loan"

rationale: A bank deposit is essentially a simple loan (mutuum) from the depositor to the bank (with the bank as debtor to the depositor for the deposit, and X as debtor to the bank for the loan); since both parties are mutually creditor and debtor of each other, for debts that are due, liquidated, and demandable, legal compensation/set-off under Art. 1278-1290 of the Civil Code is available to the bank to offset the loan against the deposit upon X's default.

source.center: CPA Review School of the Philippines (CPAR)

canonicalConcept: Because a bank deposit is legally a loan from the depositor to the bank, the bank may exercise legal compensation to set off a defaulted loan against the depositor's own deposit account, since both parties are reciprocally creditor and debtor of each other.

prompt: Which phrase best completes the statement - The affidavit of good faith in a Deed of Chattel Mortgage is

choices.text: An oath where the parties swear that the mortgage is made for the purpose of securing the obligations specified and that the obligation is just and valid
An affidavit, the absence of which will vitiate the mortgage between the parties
Necessary only if the chattel being mortgaged are growing crops
A certification form the mortgagor that he is the mortgagor of the chattel

rationale: Under the Chattel Mortgage Law, the affidavit of good faith is a sworn statement by the parties that the chattel mortgage is being entered into for the purpose of securing the obligation specified in the mortgage document and that it is a just and valid obligation, and not for the purpose of defrauding creditors; while its absence affects the mortgage's validity as against third persons, it does not affect the mortgage's validity as between the parties themselves.

source.center: CPA Review School of the Philippines (CPAR)

canonicalConcept: The affidavit of good faith in a chattel mortgage is the parties' sworn statement that the mortgage secures a just and valid obligation and is not intended to defraud creditors.

prompt: In election for the Board of Trustees of non-stock corporations, members may cast as many votes as there are trustees to be elected but may not cast more than one vote for one candidate. This is true

choices.text: Unless set aside by the members in plenary session
In every case even if the Board of Trustees resolves otherwise
Unless otherwise provided in the Articles of Incorporation or in the By-Laws
In every case even if the majority of the members decide otherwise during the election

rationale: Under Sec. 88 of the RCC, in non-stock corporations, members may cast as many votes as there are trustees to be elected but may not cumulate their votes (casting more than one vote for a single candidate), UNLESS the articles of incorporation or the by-laws provide otherwise (e.g., allowing cumulative voting) — the default straight/one-vote-per-candidate rule for non-stock corporations may thus be modified only through the AOI or by-laws, not by a mere plenary or board resolution.

source.center: CPA Review School of the Philippines (CPAR)

canonicalConcept: The default rule against cumulative voting for trustees of a non-stock corporation may be modified only by an express provision in the articles of incorporation or by-laws.

prompt: The rule is that the valuation of the shares of a stockholder who exercises his appraisal rights is determined as of the day prior to the date on which the vote was taken. This is true

choices.text: Regardless of any depreciation or appreciation in the share's fair value
Regardless of any appreciation in the share's fair value
Regardless of any depreciation in the share's fair value
Only if there is no appreciation or depreciation in the share's fair value

rationale: Under Sec. 81 of the RCC, the fair value of shares for appraisal right purposes is fixed as of the day BEFORE the vote was taken, excluding any appreciation or depreciation in anticipation of the corporate action being objected to — this valuation date is fixed as a matter of law and does not vary based on whether the shares subsequently increased or decreased in value.

source.center: CPA Review School of the Philippines (CPAR)

canonicalConcept: For appraisal rights, the fair value of a dissenting stockholder's shares is fixed as of the day before the vote was taken, regardless of subsequent appreciation or depreciation in value.

prompt: X Corporation whose business purpose is to manufacture and sell vehicles, invested its funds in Y Corporation, an investment firm through a resolution of its Board of Directors. The investment grew tremendously on account of Y Corporation's excellent business judgment. But a minority stockholder in X Corporation assails the investment as ultra vires. Is he right and, if so, what is the status of the investment? Yes, it is an ultra vires act of

choices.text: The corporation itself but voidable only, subject to stockholders ratification
Its Board of Directors and thus void
Its Board of Directors but voidable only, subject to stockholders ratification
The corporation itself, and consequently void

rationale: Under Sec. 41 of the RCC, investing corporate funds in a business or purpose different from the primary purpose stated in the AOI (here, manufacturing/selling vehicles vs. an unrelated investment firm) requires the approval of the board AND the stockholders representing at least a majority of the outstanding capital stock; investing without such stockholder approval is an ultra vires act of the BOARD (since the corporation itself has the inherent legal capacity to invest, subject to the specific procedural approval requirement) — but the act is merely VOIDABLE, curable by subsequent stockholder ratification, not automatically void.

source.center: CPA Review School of the Philippines (CPAR)

canonicalConcept: A board's investment of corporate funds in a business unrelated to the corporation's primary purpose, made without the required stockholder approval, is an ultra vires act of the board that is merely voidable and curable by subsequent stockholder ratification.

prompt: In a partnership, the liability of the partners shall be joint and solidary I. Obligations in favor of partnership suppliers by virtue of sales contract; II. Obligations in favor of a partnership client for return of deposits misappropriated by one of the partners; III. Obligations in favor of a pedestrian hit by the delivery van driven by one of the partners in the course of partnership business

choices.text: I and III
II and III
I and II
I. II and III

rationale: Under Art. 1816, ordinary contractual obligations of the partnership to suppliers by virtue of a sales/purchase contract (I) are the pro rata (not solidary) liability of the general partners, since Art. 1816 expressly makes partners liable 'pro rata' for such contracts. However, under Arts. 1822-1824, obligations arising from a partner's wrongful act or misapplication of funds received in the course of partnership business (II), and obligations arising from a partner's tortious act (such as a vehicular accident) committed in the ordinary course of partnership business (III), make ALL the partners SOLIDARILY liable with the partnership.

source.center: CPA Review School of the Philippines (CPAR)

canonicalConcept: While ordinary partnership contractual debts to suppliers are the general partners' pro rata liability, obligations arising from a partner's misapplication of funds or a tortious act committed in the course of partnership business make all partners solidarily liable with the partnership.

prompt: Venus corporation is 50% owned by Filipinos and 50% owned by Germans. Legaspi Corporation is owned 60% by Venus Corporation, 25% by other Filipino citizens and the remaining interest by Italians. Does Legaspi Corporation, a public utility, comply with the minimum Filipino ownership?

choices.text: It cannot be determined
Yes under the grandfather rule test
No under grandfather rule test
No under incorporation test

rationale: Under the Grandfather Rule (applied when the corporate layering structure raises doubt as to actual Filipino ownership, especially since Venus is only 50% Filipino-owned, i.e., its Filipino equity is in doubt), the FILIPINO equity attributable to Legaspi through Venus must be traced: Legaspi's 60% Venus-held share x Venus's 50% actual Filipino ownership = only 30% Filipino equity attributable through Venus, plus the direct 25% Filipino-held shares = 55% total. Since the applicable public utility Filipino-ownership threshold is 60%, a Filipino equity of only 55% (after grandfathering through Venus's own 50% Filipino ownership) falls short of the required 60% minimum, so Legaspi Corporation does not comply.

source.center: CPA Review School of the Philippines (CPAR)

canonicalConcept: Under the Grandfather Rule, when a shareholder-corporation's own Filipino equity is in doubt (below 60%), that share must itself be broken down to trace the ultimate Filipino equity actually attributable to the investee public utility corporation.

prompt: Georgia works as a legal researcher in a Gen. Prof. Pshp receives a daily rate of PHP 800.00 as compensation. How much will she receive as compensation if the particular day where she reported for work is A regular holiday which is also her rest day

choices.text: PHP 1600
PHP 2080
PHP 2000
PHP 2040

rationale: Under DOLE labor standards rules, work rendered on a regular holiday that also falls on the employee's rest day is compensated at 260% of the basic daily wage (200% for the regular holiday, plus an additional 30% rest-day premium computed on that 200% rate). At a daily rate of P800, this computes to P800 x 2.60 = P2,080.

source.center: CPA Review School of the Philippines (CPAR)

canonicalConcept: Work performed on a regular holiday that also falls on the employee's rest day is compensated at 260% of the basic daily wage.

prompt: Using the facts in no. 34 but Georgia was required to render two additional hours of overtime work, how much will she receive as compensation if the particular day where she performed the overtime work is On her rest day

choices.text: PHP 1060
PHP 1378
PHP 1352
PHP 1690

rationale: For work rendered on an ordinary rest day (not a holiday), the basic day's pay is 130% of the daily rate: P800 x 1.30 = P1,040. The hourly rate for that rest day is P800/8 x 1.30 = P130/hour; overtime work on a rest day carries an additional 30% overtime premium on that rest-day hourly rate: P130 x 1.30 = P169/hour, for 2 hours = P338. Total compensation for the day = P1,040 + P338 = P1,378.

source.center: CPA Review School of the Philippines (CPAR)

canonicalConcept: Overtime work rendered on an ordinary rest day is paid at 130% of the rest-day hourly rate (itself 130% of the basic hourly rate), on top of the 130% pay for the regular 8 hours worked on that rest day.

prompt: The current partner of an unmarried woman who gave birth, may be able to avail of a maternity leave of

choices.text: 0 days
7 days
10 days
12 days

rationale: Under RA 11210 (Expanded Maternity Leave Law) and its IRR, the female worker's qualified partner (whether the legitimate spouse or, in the case of an unmarried woman, the child's father or the woman's current partner cohabiting with her) may be allotted up to seven (7) days of the mother's maternity leave benefits, in lieu of and as an alternative to the paternity leave benefit under RA 8187, subject to the mother's written consent.

source.center: CPA Review School of the Philippines (CPAR)

canonicalConcept: Under the Expanded Maternity Leave Law, the qualified partner of the mother (including an unmarried woman's current partner) may be allocated up to 7 days of the maternity leave benefit with the mother's written consent.

prompt: On April 1, 2026, A and B entered into a contract of partnership for the purpose of buying and selling textbooks, with the former as capitalist partner and the latter as industrial partner. It was agreed that A shall contribute 100,000 to the common fund on May 2, 2026. Upon the arrival of the designated date, A failed to deliver the contribution he promised. As a result,

choices.text: B should make a demand upon A for the delivery of his contribution to render A in default
The contract of partnership becomes void because A failed to give his contribution to the common fund
B can compel A to deliver his contribution with interest and damages without the necessity of demand
The contract of partnership was never perfected because there was no delivery of contributions by the partners

rationale: A contract of partnership is CONSENSUAL, perfected by mere consent of the parties, not a real contract requiring delivery for perfection; hence the partnership already validly exists from April 1, 2026 despite the lack of actual contribution. Under Art. 1788, a capitalist partner who fails to contribute what he promised on the agreed date automatically becomes liable for interest and damages from the very day the contribution was due, WITHOUT need of demand, since a specific date was already fixed for the contribution.

source.center: CPA Review School of the Philippines (CPAR)

canonicalConcept: A partnership is perfected by mere consent, not by actual delivery of contributions, and a capitalist partner who fails to deliver a promised contribution on a fixed date is automatically liable for interest and damages from that date, without need of demand.

prompt: The assets of the corporation as represented by its capital stock are to be maintained unimpaired that there can be no distribution of such assets among the stockholders without provision being first made for the payment of corporate debts

choices.text: Doctrine of corporate fiction
Trust fund doctrine
Doctrine of corporate opportunity
Doctrine of limited capacity

rationale: The Trust Fund Doctrine treats a corporation's subscribed capital stock as a trust fund held for the benefit of corporate creditors, which must be maintained unimpaired; it prohibits the return or distribution of corporate assets to stockholders (e.g., through dividends or share repurchases) unless adequate provision is first made for the payment of corporate debts and liabilities.

source.center: CPA Review School of the Philippines (CPAR)

canonicalConcept: The Trust Fund Doctrine treats a corporation's capital stock as a fund held in trust for creditors, preventing its distribution to stockholders without first providing for corporate debts.

prompt: One of the following acts may be performed by the executive committee of a corporation. Which is it?

choices.text: Declaration of stock dividends
Filling of vacancies in the board of directors
Distribution of cash dividend
Approval of contracts with third persons in the ordinary course of business

rationale: Under Sec. 34 of the RCC, an executive committee, if allowed by the by-laws, may act on specific matters within the board's competence in the ordinary course of business, such as approving contracts with third persons in the regular course of the corporation's business — but it CANNOT act on matters reserved exclusively to the full board, such as filling board vacancies, or on matters requiring stockholder approval, such as declaring stock dividends or amending by-laws.

source.center: CPA Review School of the Philippines (CPAR)

canonicalConcept: An executive committee may approve ordinary-course-of-business contracts with third persons, but may not act on matters exclusively reserved to the full board (such as filling board vacancies) or those requiring stockholder approval (such as declaring stock dividends).

prompt: In a contract of sale of personal property, the price of which is payable in installments, the vendor may exercise any of the following remedies, except

choices.text: Exact fulfillment of the obligation, should the vendee fail to pay any installment
Cancel the sale, showed the vendee's failure to pay cover two or more installments
Foreclose the chattel mortgage on the thing sold, if one has been constituted show the vendee's failure to pay cover two or more installments
Rescind the sale should the vendee fail to pay any installment

rationale: Under Art. 1484 (Recto Law), the vendor's remedy to CANCEL the sale (equivalent to rescission) is available only when the vendee's default covers TWO OR MORE installments, not upon failure to pay just any single installment; the remedy of exacting fulfillment, on the other hand, may be exercised upon default of even one installment.

source.center: CPA Review School of the Philippines (CPAR)

canonicalConcept: Under the Recto Law, a vendor's remedy of cancelling/rescinding an installment sale of personal property requires the vendee's default to cover at least two installments, unlike the remedy of exacting fulfillment which is available upon default of any single installment.

prompt: The board of directors of a corporation consists of nine members, where two members were removed and two have resigned, who fills up the vacancy?

choices.text: Board, if remaining members constitute a quorum
Stockholders, since some vacancies were due to removal
Stockholders, since some vacancies were due to resignation
Board, since remaining members do not constitute a quorum

rationale: Under Sec. 28 of the RCC, vacancies caused by REMOVAL of directors must be filled by the STOCKHOLDERS (not the remaining board members), regardless of whether a quorum remains; only vacancies arising from causes OTHER than removal or expiration of term (such as resignation) may be filled by the remaining directors if they still constitute a quorum. Since two of the four vacancies here resulted from removal, the entire set of vacancies must be filled by the stockholders in a meeting called for that purpose.

source.center: CPA Review School of the Philippines (CPAR)

canonicalConcept: Vacancies in the board caused by removal must always be filled by the stockholders, regardless of whether a quorum of remaining directors exists, unlike vacancies from resignation which may be filled by the remaining directors if a quorum remains.

prompt: Any director of a corporation may be removed from office by a vote of

choices.text: Majority of the members of the board
Majority of the stockholders present
2/3 of the stockholders present
2/3 of outstanding capital stock

rationale: Under Sec. 27 of the RCC, a director may be removed, with or without cause, by a vote of the stockholders holding or representing at least two-thirds (2/3) of the OUTSTANDING CAPITAL STOCK (not merely those present at the meeting), at a regular or special meeting called for the purpose.

source.center: CPA Review School of the Philippines (CPAR)

canonicalConcept: Removal of a director requires the vote of stockholders representing at least two-thirds of the corporation's outstanding capital stock, not merely two-thirds of those present at the meeting.

prompt: A, B, C and D organized a general partnership with A and B as industrial partners and C and D as capitalist partners. C contributed Php 200,000 and D contributed Php 100,000 to the common fund. By a unanimous vote of the partners, A and B were appointed as managing partners without any specification of their respective powers and duties. Later, W applied for the position of secretary and Y applied for the position of accountant of the partnership. The hiring of W was decided upon by A and B but was opposed by C and D. The hiring of W was decided by A and D but was opposed by B and C. Who can be hired by the partnership?

choices.text: Both W and Y
Neither W nor Y
Only W
Only Y

rationale: Under Art. 1801, when two or more managing partners have been appointed without specification of duties and without a stipulation that none shall act without the consent of the others, each managing partner may separately execute acts of administration, but if there is opposition from the other managing partners, the decision of the MAJORITY of the MANAGING partners shall prevail (and in case of a tie among managing partners, the matter is referred to the partners owning the controlling interest). For W's hiring: A and B (both managing partners) decided in favor, opposed only by C and D (non-managing partners) — since C and D are not managing partners, their opposition is immaterial, and the managing partners' unanimous decision (A and B) prevails, so W is validly hired. For Y's hiring, the decision was split between the managing partners themselves (A siding one way, B another, as reflected in the facts), leaving no majority among the managing partners, so Y's hiring does not proceed.

source.center: CPA Review School of the Philippines (CPAR)

canonicalConcept: Where two or more managing partners are appointed without specified duties, the decision of the majority of the managing partners themselves controls in case of disagreement, and opposition from non-managing partners is immaterial to the validity of the managing partners' unanimous decision.

prompt: A, B and C are general partners in a merchandising firm. They contributed amounts to the capital and also agreed on equal distribution of whatever net profit is realized per fiscal period. After three years of operation, however, C conveys her whole interest in the partnership to D, without the knowledge and consent of A and B. Which of the following is not correct?

choices.text: The partnership is dissolved.
D cannot interfere or participate in the management or administration of the partnership business or affairs
D shall receive the net profits to which C would have otherwise been entitled
The conveyance by C of his whole interest in the partnership did not make D a partner

rationale: Under Art. 1813, a conveyance by a partner of his whole interest in the partnership does NOT itself dissolve the partnership, nor does it entitle the assignee (D) to interfere in the management or require an accounting during the continuance of the partnership; D is merely entitled to receive the profits to which C would otherwise have been entitled, and does NOT thereby become a partner. Statement (a) — that the partnership is dissolved by this conveyance — is therefore the incorrect statement.

source.center: CPA Review School of the Philippines (CPAR)

canonicalConcept: Under Art. 1813, a partner's conveyance of his entire interest to a third person does not dissolve the partnership nor make the assignee a partner; the assignee merely receives the assigning partner's share of profits.

prompt: Which of the following obligations is not valid?

choices.text: If the debtor promises to pay as soon as she has the means to pay
If the debtor will give his car if the creditor will pass the CPA Exam and if the creditor will fail, the creditor will have sexual intercourse with the debtor for one week.
If the debtor will give his cow or will kill the friend of the creditor
If the debtor will be the mistress of the creditor or if the debtor wants will give Php 1M to the creditor

rationale: Under Art. 1183, when an alternative obligation includes an impossible or illegal prestation among the alternatives, the obligation remains valid as long as at least one prestation is valid and the debtor's choice is not effectively confined to the illegal one; but where the obligation's structure leaves fulfillment purely to the debtor's own whim (a purely potestative condition dependent solely on the debtor's will, coupled with an alternative principal prestation itself void for being immoral, i.e., being the creditor's mistress), the entire obligation is void under Arts. 1182 and 1306.

source.center: CPA Review School of the Philippines (CPAR)

canonicalConcept: An obligation whose principal prestation is itself immoral or illegal, or whose fulfillment is made to depend purely on the debtor's own will (a potestative condition), is void.

prompt: If a pregnant woman passenger of a bus were to suffer an abortion following a vehicular accident due to the gross negligence of the bus driver, she and her husband can claim as damages from the bus company for the death of their unborn child, except

choices.text: Actual damages in the form of imdemnity for the loss of life of the unborn child
Moral damages for mental anguish that attended the loss of the unborn child
Exemplary damages since there is gross negligence
Actual damages for the bodily injury she suffered from the loss of the fetus which is considered part of her internal organs.

rationale: Philippine jurisprudence (following Geluz v. CA and related cases) holds that an unborn child who dies before birth (without ever having had juridical personality, since civil personality is acquired only upon birth under Art. 40-41) cannot be the subject of an indemnity for 'loss of life,' since it never had a legal personality or life recognized by law to be indemnified for; the parents may, however, recover moral damages for their own mental anguish, exemplary damages given the driver's gross negligence, and actual damages for the mother's own bodily injury (the physical harm/loss she personally suffered).

source.center: CPA Review School of the Philippines (CPAR)

canonicalConcept: Because an unborn child who dies before birth never acquires juridical/civil personality under the Civil Code, there can be no indemnity for 'loss of life' of the unborn child, though the parents may still recover moral, exemplary, and the mother's own actual bodily-injury damages.

Obligations in favor of a partnership client for return of deposits misappropriated by one of the partners III. Obligations in favor of a pedestrian hit by the delivery van driven by one of the partners in the course of partnership business

choices.text: I and III
II and III
I and II
I, II and III

rationale: Under Art. 1816, ordinary contractual obligations of the partnership to suppliers by virtue of a sales/purchase contract (I) are the pro rata (not solidary) liability of the general partners. However, under Arts. 1822-1824, obligations arising from a partner's wrongful act or misapplication of funds received in the course of partnership business (II), and obligations arising from a partner's tortious act (such as a vehicular accident) committed in the ordinary course of partnership business (III), make ALL the partners SOLIDARILY liable with the partnership.

source.center: CPA Review School of the Philippines (CPAR)

canonicalConcept: While ordinary partnership contractual debts to suppliers are the general partners' pro rata liability, obligations arising from a partner's misapplication of funds or a tortious act committed in the course of partnership business make all partners solidarily liable with the partnership.

prompt: Which of the following statements is false?

choices.text: Treasury shares revert to the unissued shares of the corporation and being in the treasury they don't have the status of outstanding shares
Shares issued without par value shall be deemed fully paid and non assessable and the holder of such shares shall not be liable to the corporation or its creditors in respect thereto

Redeemable shares may be redeemed regardless of the existence of unrestricted retained earnings provided such redemption would not cause insolvency or inability of the corporation to meet its debts as they mature
When par value shares are issued above par, the premium or excess is not to be considered as part of the legal capital

rationale: Treasury shares are shares that have been issued, fully paid for, and subsequently REACQUIRED by the corporation; they do NOT revert to the status of unissued shares (they remain 'issued' shares, merely held in the treasury), which is what makes choice (a) false. Treasury shares do lose their status as OUTSTANDING shares while held by the corporation, but they remain part of the 'issued' shares — the false part of statement (a) is treating them as reverting to 'unissued' shares.

source.center: CPA Review School of the Philippines (CPAR)

canonicalConcept: Treasury shares remain issued shares of the corporation even while held in treasury (merely losing outstanding-share status), and do not revert to unissued-share status.

prompt: Which of the following statements is correct?

choices.text: When a vacancy in the board arises, such vacancy maybe filled by the remaining directors provided they still constitute a quorum
The officers of a non-stock corporation maybe elected directly by the members instead of by the board of trustees
The number of trustees in a non-stock corporation maybe five (5) but not more than fifteen (15)
A director individually and acting as such can bind the corporation because he is an agent of the corporation

rationale: Under Sec. 92 of the RCC, in a non-stock corporation, corporate officers may be directly elected by the members themselves, if so provided in the articles of incorporation or by-laws, rather than by the board of trustees as is the usual rule; choice (a) is over-generalized (vacancies from removal or expiration of term still require a stockholders'/members' vote), (c) is incorrect (non-stock trustees may exceed 15, per Sec. 13), and (d) is incorrect (an individual director has no power to bind the corporation on his own; only the board acting as a body, or a duly authorized officer/agent, may do so).

source.center: CPA Review School of the Philippines (CPAR)

canonicalConcept: Under the RCC, a non-stock corporation may provide in its articles of incorporation or by-laws for its officers to be elected directly by the members, rather than by the board of trustees.

prompt: As regards cash dividend, which of the following is correct?

choices.text: Declared by the board by majority vote and ratified by the stockholders by majority vote
Declared by the board by majority vote and ratified by the stockholders by ⅔ vote of the outstanding capital stock
Declared by the board by majority vote and need not be ratified by the stockholders
Declared by the board by ⅔ vote and need not be ratified by the stockholders

rationale: Cash dividends may be declared by the board of directors alone, by a mere majority vote of the quorum present at a board meeting, WITHOUT need of stockholder ratification or approval — unlike STOCK dividends, which additionally require the approval of stockholders representing at least 2/3 of the outstanding capital stock at a meeting called for the purpose.

source.center: CPA Review School of the Philippines (CPAR)

canonicalConcept: Cash dividends require only a majority vote of the board of directors, with no need for stockholder ratification, unlike stock dividends which require an additional 2/3 stockholder approval.

prompt: Which of the following statements is not correct?

choices.text: An agreement to constitute a commodatum is binding and is perfected from the moment there is meeting of minds
Fixed, savings, and current deposits of money in banks and similar institutions shall be governed by the provisions concerning mutuum.
Precarium is a kind of commodatum where the bailor may demand the thing loaned at will
In case of extraordinary expenses, the debtor in mutuum will shoulder 50% if he is in actual use of the thing borrowed.

rationale: A contract of MUTUUM (simple loan of money or fungibles) transfers OWNERSHIP of the thing loaned to the borrower, so there is no concept of shared 'extraordinary expenses' between lender and borrower as in a commodatum — this sharing rule (Art. 1949, borrower shoulders 50% of extraordinary expenses for preservation of the thing if he is in actual use of it, subject to reimbursement) applies specifically to COMMODATUM, not to mutuum, making statement (d) the incorrect one. (Choice a correctly states commodatum is consensual/perfected by meeting of minds even though delivery is needed for the loan itself to arise; choice b correctly reflects Art. 1980; choice c correctly describes precarium under Art. 1947.)

source.center: CPA Review School of the Philippines (CPAR)

canonicalConcept: The rule on sharing extraordinary preservation expenses (borrower shoulders 50% if using the thing even against the lender's will) applies specifically to commodatum, not to mutuum, where ownership of the loaned fungibles passes entirely to the borrower.

prompt: A and B are co-owners of a parcel of land from where they share the profits equally as co-heirs in inheritance. Is there a partnership?

choices.text: There is a prima facie presumption of partnership because of the equal sharing of profits
There is no partnership because co-ownership by itself does not establish a partnership despite the sharing of profits
There is no partnership since in partnership, division of profits is not always necessary among partners
There is prima facie presumption of partnership they being co-owners and co-possessors

rationale: Under Art. 1769(2), co-ownership or co-possession, by itself, does not establish a partnership, whether or not the co-owners share any profits made by the use of the property they jointly own — this is an express statutory exception to the general prima facie presumption of partnership from profit-sharing, precisely to cover situations like co-heirs jointly holding inherited property.

source.center: CPA Review School of the Philippines (CPAR)

canonicalConcept: Co-ownership or co-possession, even with sharing of profits from the co-owned property, does not by itself establish a partnership under Art. 1769(2) of the Civil Code.

prompt: H, an Olympic judo champion, with violence and intimidation forced his wife W to sell W's pieces of jewelry to B. The sale is

choices.text: Valid and binding
Voidable, because the consent of W is vitiated
Rescissible, if W suffered lesion of more than ¼ of the value of the property
Void, except when a separation of property was agreed upon in the marriage settlement or there has been a judicial separation of property

rationale: The violence and intimidation vitiating W's consent were exerted by H, her husband, and not by B, the buyer, who is not shown to have known of or participated in that coercion; since the sale of W's exclusive jewelry was made to an innocent third party (B), the external contract of sale between W and B is treated as valid and binding as far as B is concerned, with W's proper remedy for the vitiated consent lying against H (the one who employed the violence and intimidation), not against the innocent buyer B.

source.center: CPA Review School of the Philippines (CPAR)

canonicalConcept: Where violence or intimidation vitiating a seller's consent is exerted by a third person (not the buyer), and the buyer had no knowledge of or participation in the coercion, the resulting sale to that innocent buyer may still be treated as valid and binding as between seller and buyer.

prompt: Statement 1- A director is removed from office by a vote of the stockholders holding or representing at least 2/3 of outstanding capital stock. The vacancy occasioned by such removal can be filled by the vote of at least a majority of the remaining directors if still constituting a quorum. Statement 2- Treasury shares sold for less than par or issued value are considered "watered stock" and as such are prohibited by law.

choices.text: True, true
True, false
False, true
False, false

rationale: Statement 1 is false: a vacancy caused by REMOVAL of a director must be filled by the STOCKHOLDERS themselves (Sec. 28, RCC), not by the remaining board members, regardless of whether a quorum remains. Statement 2 is also false: treasury shares, having already been fully paid for upon their original issuance, may validly be resold below their original par/issued price without constituting 'watered stock,' since watered stock refers to shares originally ISSUED for less than par/issued value or for inadequate consideration, not to a corporation's resale of its own previously-fully-paid treasury shares at a discount.

source.center: CPA Review School of the Philippines (CPAR)

canonicalConcept: A board vacancy caused by removal must be filled by the stockholders, not the remaining directors, and treasury shares (already fully paid upon original issuance) may be resold below par without constituting watered stock.

The names of the manufacturers are apparently different as printed on the bottom part of their labels. However, the label designs, colors, print styles and sizes are very similar and almost identical. What test shall be applied to determine if there is a trademark infringement?
